title: Integrated Mobility and Affordability Plan
executive_summary: Reduce downtown traffic congestion, improve housing access, and protect the city budget without worsening pollution.

policy_goal.statement: Reduce weekday downtown traffic congestion by 20% within 18 months, improve housing access for working residents, and keep the city's annual operating budget in surplus.

problem_statement: Metroville has heavy peak-hour congestion downtown, rising housing costs, aging transit infrastructure, and pollution spillover from Industrial East into Residential North. These linked pressures affect mobility, affordability, health, and public trust in city governance.
objectives: Improve commuting time for working residents.
Increase housing affordability near jobs and transit.
Avoid turning the current budget surplus into a structural deficit.
Reduce pollution exposure in residential areas.

policy_package.title: Transit upgrade
policy_package.description: Modernize one major bus corridor and add one express shuttle connection between Residential North and Downtown Commercial.

policy_package.title: Parking reform
policy_package.description: Raise downtown parking prices during peak hours and convert selected curb space into bus priority lanes.

policy_package.title: Housing incentive
policy_package.description: Allow mid-rise mixed-use housing near transit nodes with affordability requirements for part of the new stock.

policy_package.title: Industrial mitigation
policy_package.description: Require emissions-control upgrades for the highest-polluting industrial sites and add green buffers near Residential North.

policy_package.title: Public communication campaign
policy_package.description: Explain the short-term disruption, expected benefits, and timeline to residents and businesses.

budget.tax_policy: No new broad-based tax increase in year one

constraints: No mass layoffs in city departments.
Maintain annual budget surplus if possible.
Avoid policies that sharply increase commute burdens for low-income workers.
Deliver visible public progress within 12 months.
stakeholders: City budget office and elected leadership
key_tradeoffs: Better transit and affordability may require upfront capital spending.
Parking reform can reduce congestion but may trigger business opposition.
Industrial mitigation improves health but can create employer resistance.
Housing near transit improves access but may face neighborhood pushback.
success_metrics: Net budget impact after 12 and 18 months
